entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Zdeněk Matějček was a Czech child psychologist, researcher, and childcare reformer, who pioneered the study of the institutional conditions of raising children in an environment of psychological deprivation. He was a significant reformer of child care, emphasising the irreplaceable role of the family. He was known for studies of the effects on children of being held in prison camps during World War II, was a co-founder and the first chairman of an association that involved animals, such as dogs and horses, in child therapy, and was the principal organizer of a meeting of the International Association for Research in Learning Disabilities, held in Prague on 2–5 October 1989.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Zdeněk Matějček's research on the effects of institutional care on children in prison camps during World War II informed modern child psychology and highlighted the importance of family as a primary caregiver. His work contributed to the development of animal-assisted therapy for children with learning disabilities.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a pioneer in child psychology and childcare reform, Matějček's work had significant regional impact on Eastern Europe during World War II, influencing post-war policies on child welfare. His research on the effects of institutional care on children has been cited by subsequent studies on child development.
